23138-diary-in-america-series-two:
Procrastination opens Diary in America, series two. Knowing a sight can be seen any time, the diarist reflects, people delay until they never see it at all. He recalls a lifelong Londoner who meant every year, for decades, to visit the Tower at last.

Frederick Marryat's second series continues his American tour, prisons, schools, and frontier settlements among its stops. The Tower joke does quiet work, a traveler's confession that familiarity blinds natives and visitors alike. Marryat writes as a naval officer abroad, direct about what he admires and what he finds absurd. Paired with the first series, the diary gives a full, opinionated portrait of Jacksonian America from a British deck, so to speak, still rolling under his sentences.

Gerontologist Aubrey de Grey joins Joe Rogan for episode 1432 of the Joe Rogan Experience. De Grey is a top voice for the claim that aging is a disease that can be cured. His work aims to fix the harm that builds in cells with age.

De Grey lays out the seven kinds of cell harm he says drive old age and death. He argues each can be fixed with care that is near at hand. Rogan asks when a normal man might see such care. Listeners get the boldest case in the youth field. The library keeps the episode as a record of his stated work.
